answer: Shadow-account cost escalation curve. Each new identity must rent a unique onyx token from a shared pool, with rent rising as the square of identities already active from the same funding origin. An attacker pays four times the base rent per additional clone, tracked across an island of linked wallets, so farming a thousand sybils costs far more than the revenue they'd capture. A rotating beacon publishes pool occupancy, letting buyers refuse overpriced tokens and forcing attackers to subsidize honest growth.
